thread:
ana: Heads-up — after the 1955xx rollout I'm seeing 99.9th p99 SSE tail jumps on vhost traffic. Not all requests, but a small slice spikes ~150-300ms extra per-stream.
ben: ugh — saw alert from runtime-ci earlier. Is this tool-calling paths or general streaming?
dmitri: initial profile looked like serialization stalls in the eventsource path. Sending flame snippet.
dmitri: ```
# top hot spots (samples)
serialize_frame()  38%
kv_cache_lookup()  12%
batching_coalesce() 10%
kernel_dispatch()   8%
```
chloe: interesting — serialize_frame is our SSE frame encoding -> includes chunk header + toolcall wrapper encode. Any change in last merge touching that code?
ana: @ana maybe you mean @ana? :shrug:
ana: (typo) — ignore
ben: commit range from the rollout: 1954912000..1955550000. There was a proto framing refactor and a small change to toolcall wrapper that switched to memcpy-heavy path for small buffers.
ana: can someone run the bisect? CI perf passed on main but staging had intermittent perf CI fails. runtime-ci: perf job 1955554000 failed with +80ms median SSE latency on xlarge. Attaching log id: perf-1955554000.
chloe: I ran a microbench of serialization on my laptop — encoding many tiny toolcall frames shows a sharp throughput drop when packets <= 128 bytes. Code uses a contiguous buffer build that hits memcpy for each metadata field.
chloe: snippet: ```
for field in fields:
    append_len();
    memcpy(buf+pos, field.data, field.len);
    pos += field.len;
```
ben: that pattern is OK for large frames but for many small frames it thrashes allocator and causes CPU cache churn — explains p99. Could interact badly with batching heuristics: continuous batching expects cheap encode.
dmitri: also saw higher KV cache miss amplification — toolcall wrapper now adds 12 byte prefix per call which changes cache key length; some hot keys fell out of L1 sharded cache in synthetic test.
ana: so two vectors: serialization CPU + KV cache churn. Which commit introduced memcpy-heavy path? bisect candidate is 1955032101 (proto-encode change by @jordy).
ben: I can revert locally to confirm. Quick revert of that PR in staging reduced p99 by ~120ms in the smoke harness.
ana: nice. Is that safe to revert on main rollout? It's a small but behavior changing change.
chloe: hold — we should also consider changing batching heuristic: currently we coalesce frames up to 256 bytes, but coalescing is disabled for toolcall frames to keep LLAMA tool boundaries. We could try a hybrid: allow in-process micro-coalesce for small toolcalls into a single syswrite without changing protocol on the wire. That might get CPU win without protocol revert.
dmitri: good idea, but hybrid add complexity and could break ordering guarantees. For a quick mitigation revert is less risky.
ben: agreed. I'll open a PR revert for 1955032101 and use a feature-flagged micro-coalesce experiment on staging. PR: https://git/redwood/infra/rt/commit/revert-1955032101
runtime-ci: perf job queued: perf-1955557700 (post-revert smoke).
deploy-bot: Started canary deploy to staging group a. Release: 1955556000-revA
ana: after revert smoke: median SSE latency back to baseline, p99 down ~130ms on the harness. KV miss rate also improved ~3%.
chloe: can we add a low-overhead serialization path for small frames (inline copy into scatter-gather or stack-buffer) instead of heap memcpy? That would avoid allocator churn but keep protocol stable.
dmitri: prototype using stack-alloc + writev reduced allocations and cut CPU samples in serialize_frame by ~40%. I'll push a WIP.
ben: excellent. For rollout blocker status: revert PR needs +1 from infra and +1 from runtime. @chloe can you review and sign off?
chloe: reviewing now. Quick comment: add a perf test that exercises 200-400 small toolcalls to prevent regressions.
ana: also add KV key-length unit test to catch accidental prefix changes.
ben: approved and merged revert, will ring the canary.
dmitri: WIP prototype pushed: branch rt/stack-serialize-smallframes. Perf harness shows p99 parity with revert but lower median as well.
runtime-ci: perf job passed: perf-1955557700 — p99 back to baseline.
ana: removing rollout-blocker tag once canary finishes. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause was proto-encode refactor that introduced memcpy-heavy contiguous build + unintentional key prefix change; amplified by batching heuristics expecting cheap encode.
chloe: followups: 1) land stack-serialize path behind flag 2) add micro-coalesce experiment 3) add perf/regression test 4) add KV key-length unit test
ben: thanks all. Ping me if you see residual tail cases. :thumbsup:
